source: FICTIONAL desktop-PC maintenance simulation. Illustrative only - not real maintenance advice. Hardware facts to be validated against an equipment source before the main study.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU rocker switch at the rear of the case to O (off).
steps.explanation: The switch isolates mains power from the motherboard. The board still carries standby voltage while the switch is on, so nothing is touched before this.

steps.instruction: Touch the bare metal ground point to discharge static.
steps.explanation: Static electricity from your body can harm the fan's bearing electronics. Grounding once, before the case is opened, covers the whole job.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the top-left panel thumbscrew.
steps.explanation: The panel is held by four thumbscrews, one at each corner. They are hand-tight, so no tools are needed.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the top-right panel thumbscrew.
steps.explanation: Each thumbscrew is loosened individually. Removing them one at a time keeps the panel seated until all four are free.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the bottom-right panel thumbscrew.
steps.explanation: Thumbscrews stay captive in the panel, so they cannot roll into the case or get lost.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the bottom-left panel thumbscrew.
steps.explanation: With the last screw free the panel is only held by the slots along the case edge.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel off to open the case.
steps.explanation: The panel rides on slots along the case edge. Sliding it back first, then lifting, avoids bending the sheet metal.

steps.instruction: Unplug the front fan's cable from the SYS_FAN header.
steps.explanation: The fan's power and tachometer lines run through this header. Unplugging first means no wire is stretched when the fan comes out.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the fan's top-left corner screw.
steps.explanation: The fan is held by four screws, one at each corner. Loosening them one at a time keeps the fan from dropping.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the fan's top-right corner screw.
steps.explanation: Each corner screw carries part of the fan's weight until all four are free.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the fan's bottom-left corner screw.
steps.explanation: Fan screws are short and self-tapping; keeping them in order makes refitting easy.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the fan's bottom-right corner screw.
steps.explanation: With the last screw free the fan is only resting against the mounting frame.

steps.instruction: Lift the old fan out of the mounting frame.
steps.explanation: The fan comes straight out of its frame once all four screws are free and the cable is unplugged.

steps.instruction: Seat the replacement fan in the mounting frame.
steps.explanation: The fan's corners line up with the four screw holes in the frame. The airflow arrow on its side points toward the back of the case.

steps.instruction: Screw in the fan's top-left corner screw.
steps.explanation: Each screw is started loosely first, then tightened, so the fan sits square in the frame.

steps.instruction: Screw in the fan's top-right corner screw.
steps.explanation: Tightening opposite corners in turn keeps the fan frame from twisting.

steps.instruction: Screw in the fan's bottom-left corner screw.
steps.explanation: A loose corner screw lets the fan vibrate, which is the noise a failing fan makes.

steps.instruction: Screw in the fan's bottom-right corner screw.
steps.explanation: All four corners secured, the fan is held firmly against its rubber mounts.

steps.instruction: Plug the fan's cable back into the SYS_FAN header.
steps.explanation: The header is keyed so the plug only fits one way. Without it the fan never spins.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel back on until it clicks home.
steps.explanation: Closing the case before power is restored keeps dust out and the airflow path intact.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU power switch back to I (on).
steps.explanation: Power is restored only after every part is secured, and the new fan spins up on the next start.

hazard.message: STATIC WARNING: charge detected on your wrist. Discharge on the case metal before touching the fan!
